incident.headline: Re-entry widens, hotspots remain
incident.summary: The situation is now materially better than yesterday: re-entry has expanded to Biganos and Audenge, Lacanau campsites and other tourist accommodation may reopen, and rail traffic south of Bordeaux is expected to resume progressively from Saturday. But this is not a clean all-clear. Le Monde’s current live index still flags several hotspots around Cap Ferret and Lacanau, and the larger Gironde fire remains a managed, staged-recovery emergency rather than a normal summer-access situation.

currentAssessment.verdict: The regional picture is improving: Biganos, Audenge and Lacanau tourist accommodation are moving into staged return/reopening, and rail south of Bordeaux is expected to resume progressively from Saturday. The caution is that hotspots still persist around Cap Ferret and Lacanau, so this remains staged recovery, not a simple all-clear.
currentAssessment.trajectory: Improving staged recovery, with local hotspots still active
currentAssessment.narrative: The important update today is that staged return is broadening beyond yesterday’s first wave. Le Monde’s 15:46 live index says residents of Biganos and Audenge can return, adding to twelve communes already covered by re-entry measures, and that residents of Lacanau campsites, tourist residences and holiday villages are also authorised to come back. That is a real improvement for Bassin/Lacanau access and the tourism layer. At the same time, the same current live index says several hotspots persist around Cap Ferret and Lacanau, which keeps the operational picture fragile. Separate current reporting from Sud Ouest says rail traffic south of Bordeaux can resume progressively from Saturday. For Cap Ferret, the dashboard should now read as cautious improvement: better regional movement, but still wait for explicit local access and visitor instructions before treating the peninsula as normally open.
currentAssessment.confidence: High confidence that the Biganos/Audenge and Lacanau return update is material because it appears in the current Le Monde live index and is corroborated by RTL and regional live reporting. High confidence that this is not yet a blanket all-clear because the same evidence still reports hotspots around Cap Ferret and Lacanau. Moderate confidence on rail timing until SNCF’s operational resumption is visible in transport services on Saturday.

closure.status: Elevated risk · flights operating but heavily disrupted
closure.detail: The official board still lists arrivals and departures, but it flags 1 delayed and 0 cancelled arrivals, plus 0 delayed and 0 cancelled departures. The airport's own flash notice says activity continues, while the hotel zone around the airport is evacuated until further notice and the halls close overnight, so the site cannot provide accommodation. Treat flight operation, terminal overnight access and ground access as separate signals.

groundAccess.status: Road/taxi access possible but disrupted · check live routing

Check live navigation and taxi availability before leaving.

Les résidents des campings, résidences de tourisme et villages vacances situés sur la commune de Lacanau sont également autorisés à revenir. Plusieurs points chauds persistent autour du Cap-Ferret et de Lacanau.

Une modification du territoire qui a pu augmenter le risque d’incendie, et la difficulté pour les pompiers de combattre le feu, analyse, dans un entretien au « Monde », la géographe Christine Bouisset.

Incendie en Gironde : à la préfecture de Bordeaux, une gestion de crise « jour et nuit » Depuis neuf jours, le centre opérationnel départemental, dans la capitale girondine, coordonne vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre la gestion du mégafeu, qui a dévasté 42 000 hectares. La cellule de crise regroupe tous les services impliqués dans le sinistre. Jeudi 30 juillet au soir, les points chauds étaient moins nombreux.

Au CHU de Bordeaux, une organisation millimétrée pour faire face à l’impact de l’incendie : « Si on a tenu, c’est grâce à la solidarité hospitalière » Cellule de crise quotidienne, ouverture de lits, appel aux volontaires… A l’hôpital Pellegrin, centre opérationnel de la prise en charge sanitaire, l’adaptation aux conséquences du mégafeu qui touche la Gironde depuis le 22 juillet s’est faite au jour le jour, selon les besoins.

« La France brûle » : la presse européenne s’inquiète des incendies en Gironde et pointe l’absence de débat sur les « causes profondes » des feux Les incendies qui ravagent la forêt girondine sont suivis de près par les médias des pays voisins. Quelque 3 300 sapeurs-pompiers sont toujours mobilisés dans le département, ainsi que 1 500 militaires, 1 250 policiers et gendarmes et 24 moyens aériens. Les pompiers en Gironde se disent « raisonnablement optimistes » après une nuit calme.

officialCheckpoints.title: Prefecture point · 16:00
